title: Reading the Mobile Viewport
reading_goal: Understand the concept of the viewport so that the app is displayed to fit the width of the mobile screen.
question: What is the purpose of the mobile viewport setting?
choices: To display the page according to the width of the mobile screen,
answer: To display the page according to the width of the mobile screen,
explanation: width=device-width and initial-scale=1 align the layout viewport with device width so responsive CSS behaves as expected. Do not block pinch zoom with user-scalable=no or a restrictive maximum-scale. The viewport tag alone does not create a responsive layout.

title: Read about responsive layouts
reading_goal: Understand responsive layouts, where the arrangement of cards changes depending on the screen size.
question: What is the purpose of a responsive layout?
choices: To adjust the UI layout to fit the screen size,
answer: To adjust the UI layout to fit the screen size,
explanation: Since PCs and mobile phones have different screen widths, even the same card must be designed with different sizes and margins. A responsive layout is a structure where the layout changes depending on the screen size. On mobile devices, button size, line breaks, and scroll flow have a significant impact on actual usability.

title: Reading "Touch Target"
reading_goal: Understand the concept of touch targets, which ensures buttons are large enough to be easily pressed with a finger.
question: Why is "touch target" important?
choices: To make it easier to press the button accurately with your finger,
answer: To make it easier to press the button accurately with your finger,
explanation: A 44 CSS-pixel minimum height plus padding is a starting point for a larger hit area. Also check width, spacing, device behavior, and applicable accessibility guidance on real touch hardware. A visually large control can still have a small clickable child or be covered by an overlay.

title: Reading Tap Target Spacing
reading_goal: I understand that sufficient spacing is required between touch targets.
question: What is the purpose of tap target spacing?
choices: To reduce the number of times you accidentally press nearby buttons,
answer: To reduce the number of times you accidentally press nearby buttons,
explanation: Tap target spacing refers to the distance between tap targets. When card options are arranged side by side on mobile devices, the spacing tends to be too narrow, making accidental taps more likely. Leaving sufficient spacing can help reduce the likelihood of accidentally tapping an adjacent option when tapping with your finger.

title: Read the thumb zone
reading_goal: Understand the concept of the "thumb zone," which takes into account the area that is easily reached by the thumb.
question: Why is the thumb zone taken into account?
choices: To make common mobile gestures more convenient,
answer: To make common mobile gestures more convenient,
explanation: The thumb zone is the area of the screen that your thumb can comfortably reach. Repetitive actions—such as swiping to the next card or checking the answer—should be easier to access than search functions. On mobile devices, buttons in hard-to-reach areas may see lower usage rates, so we check the placement of key buttons first.

title: Reading: Hover vs. Touch
reading_goal: I understand that relying solely on mouse hover can cause information to disappear on touch devices.
question: Why shouldn't we rely solely on hover?
choices: Since touch devices either don't support hover or it behaves differently,
answer: Since touch devices either don't support hover or it behaves differently,
explanation: "Hover vs. touch" refers to the difference between hovering a mouse over an element and touching it with a finger. If hints or explanations are only visible on hover, mobile learners will have difficulty accessing them. In a touch environment, alternative UI elements are needed—such as when tapped, when expanded, or when always visible. Therefore, the correct answer is “Because hover does not exist or behaves differently on touch devices.”
